source_text: Ἵνα δὲ μή τινες ἀλογισταίνοντες εἰς ἀποτροπὴν τῶν δεδιδαγμένων ὑφ᾿ ἡμῶν εἴπωσι πρὸ ἐτῶν ἑκατὸν πεκτήκοντα γεγεννῆσθαι τὸν Χριστὸν λέγειν ἡμᾶς ἐπὶ Κυρηνίου, δεδιδαχέναι δὲ ἅ φαμεν διδάξαι αὐτὸν ὕστερον χρόνοις ἐπὶ Ποντίου Πιλάτου, καὶ ἐπικαλῶσιν ὡς ἀνευθύνων ὄντων τῶν προγεγενημένων πάντων ἀνθρώπων, φθάσαντες τὴν ἀπορίαν λυσόμεθα. Τὸν Χριστὸν πρωτότοκον τοῦ θεοῦ εἶναι ἐδιδάχθημεν καὶ προεμηνύσαμεν λόγον ὄντα, οἷ πᾶν γένος ἀνθρώπων μετέσχε. Καὶ οἱ μετὰ λόγου βιώσαντες Χριστιανοί εἰσι, κἂν ἄθεοι ἐνομίσθησαν, οἷον ἐν Ἕλλησι μὲν Σωκράτης καὶ Ἡράκλειτος καὶ οἱ ὅμοιοι αὐτοῖς, ἐν βαρβάροις δὲ Αβραὰμ καὶ Ἀνανίας καὶ Ἀζαρίας καὶ Μισαὴλ καὶ Ἡλίας καὶ ἄλλοι πολλοί, ὧν τὰς πράξεις ἢ τὰ ὀνόματα καταλέγειν μακρὸν εἶναι ἐπιστάμενοι τανῦν παραιτούμεθα. Ὥστε καὶ οἱ προγενόμενοι ἄνευ λόγου βιάσαντες ἄχρηστοι καὶ ἐχθροὶ τῷ Χριστῷ ἦσαν καὶ φονεῖς τῶν μετὰ λόγου βιούντων· οἱ δὲ μετὰ λόγου βιώσαντες καὶ βιοῦντες Χριστιανοὶ καὶ ἄφοβοι καὶ ἀτάραχοι ὑπάρχσυσι. Δι᾿ ἣν αἰτίαν διὰ δυνάμεως τοῦ λόγου κατὰ τὴν τοῦ πατρὸς πάντων καὶ δεσπότου θεοῖ βουλὴν διὰ παρθένου ἄνθρωπος ἀπεκυήθη καὶ Ἰησοῦς ἐπωνομάσθη, καὶ σταυρωθεὶς καὶ ἀποθανὼν ἀνέστη καὶ ἀνελήλυθεν εἰς οὐρανὸν, ἐκ τῶν διὰ τοσούτων εἰρημένων ὁ νουνεχὴς καταλαβεῖν δυνήσεται. Ἡμεῖς δέ, οὐκ ἀναγκαίου ὄντος τανῦν τοῖ περὶ τῆς ἀποδείξεως τούτου λόγου, ἐπὶ τὰς ἐπειγούσας ἀποδείξεις πρὸς τὸ παρὸν χωρήσομεν.
pass_a_gloss: So that some unreasoning people may not turn away from the teachings given by us, saying that we say Christ was born one hundred and fifty years ago under Cyrenius, but that we say the things he taught were taught by him later in the time of Pontius Pilate, and they call upon the fact that all people before him were unaccountable, we will resolve the difficulty. We were taught that Christ is the firstborn of God and that he is the Word, in whom all humanity has a share. And those who have lived according to the Word are Christians, even if they were considered atheists, such as Socrates and Heraclitus among the Greeks, and Abraham and Ananias and Azarias and Misael and Elijah and many others among the barbarians, whose deeds or names we know it would be long to recount, so we omit them for now. So, those who lived before him without the Word were useless and enemies of Christ and killers of those who lived according to the Word; but those who lived and live according to the Word are Christians and are fearless and untroubled. For this reason, through the power of the Word, according to the plan of the Father of all, the Master God, a man was born of a virgin and was named Jesus, and was crucified and died and rose again and ascended into heaven, from the things that have been said so far, the intelligent person will be able to understand. But we, since it is not necessary now to deal with the proofs of this, will turn to the urgent proofs for the present.
pass_b_english: We resolve this difficulty so that no unreasoning person may turn away from our teachings by claiming we say Christ was born one hundred fifty years ago under Cyrenius, that he taught only later under Pontius Pilate, and that all who lived before him were unaccountable. We were taught that Christ is the firstborn of God, the Word in whom all humanity shares. Those who live by the Word are Christians, even if the world called them atheists — Socrates and Heraclitus among the Greeks; Abraham, Ananias, Azarias, Misael, Elijah, and countless others among the nations. To recount their deeds or names would be long, so we pass over them now. Therefore, those who lived before Christ without the Word were useless, enemies of Christ, and murderers of those who lived by the Word; but those who live and have lived by the Word are Christians, fearless and untroubled. For this reason, by the power of the Word and according to the will of the Father of all, the Master God, a man was born of a virgin and named Jesus; he was crucified, died, rose again, and ascended into heaven. From all this the intelligent person can understand. Since it is not necessary now to rehearse the proofs of this, we turn to the urgent proofs at hand.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text, including the complex conditional structure regarding the historical timeline of Christ's birth and teaching. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the Greek source. All names and theological distinctions (firstborn of God, Word, Father/Master God) are preserved.

Pass A: 'We were taught that Christ is the firstborn of God and that he is the Word, in whom all humanity has a share.' Pass B: 'We were taught that Christ is the firstborn of God, the Word in whom all humanity shares.'
